svg.title: Vaibik — USB-powered breadboard wiring
svg.desc: Exact reference wiring for a nice!nano v2-compatible nRF52840 transmitter, Adafruit PDM microphone breakout 3492, and normally open PTT switch. The microphone uses 3.3 volts, common ground, SEL to ground, CLK P0.17 and DAT P0.20. PTT P0.06 switches to ground. A separate receiver connects to the computer by USB and communicates by 2.4 GHz radio. No signal wire links the two boards.
svg.text: USB-powered bench prototype · exact wiring reference · no battery or enclosure
Rails unused. A–E share a row; F–J share a row. Center channel separates them.
Internal pull-up. Pressing connects P0.06 to GND.
Use diagonal switch legs; verify the contact pairs with a meter.
SEL is grounded explicitly for the left PDM channel.
Insulated wire crossings do not form electrical junctions.
1 USB at top. Follow P0.xx pin IDs; clone silkscreen can differ.
2 Mount PDM pins J6–J10 in five different rows. Leave its acoustic port clear.
3 Lower two unused controller pins overhang the breadboard; insulate them.
3.3 V ONLY at the microphone. Never use RAW / BAT+ / 5 V.
Reference drawing; physical assembly still needs a bench test.
